title: skim
description: skim: peers, latency, RPC, the state your calls read, and what skim serves back.

panels.title: Head age
panels.description: Time since the head block's slot started. Above one slot (12 s) means skim is behind.

panels.title: Block arrival P50 (15m)
panels.description: Payload gossip arrival after slot start.

panels.title: SNAP state peers
panels.description: EL peers that serve state skim doesn't hold. 0 means on-demand reads wait (--state-wait).

panels.title: Addresses not fully pinned
panels.description: Addresses your calls read that no subscription fully pins (see State and addresses).

panels.title: Block arrival after slot start
panels.description: When the execution payload reached skim over consensus gossip, relative to its slot start (5 m windows).

panels.title: SNAP latency per peer (EWMA)
panels.description: Point-lookup latency per state peer, from skim's adaptive fetch scheduler.

panels.title: SNAP fetch scheduler
panels.description: failed = a key no peer could serve in time (the request got -32002).

panels.title: First SNAP peer
panels.description: Until a SNAP-capable peer connects, state skim doesn't hold can't be fetched (requests wait up to --state-wait).

panels.title: SNAP peers held 60 s
panels.description: Many SNAP peers drop skim within a minute because they are full; these stayed. Held peers rank first in the saved list.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: reth network manager: sessions, known peers, dials in progress.

panels.title: Disconnect reasons (outbound)
panels.description: Why sessions skim dialed ended. too_many_peers = the remote was full (common on Sepolia).

panels.title: Outcomes
panels.description: unavailable = -32002 (state or data no peer could serve); reverted = execution reverted.

panels.title: Addresses your calls read
panels.description: Every address eth_call executions read (top --metrics-addresses). pinned = kept current by a subscription; on demand = fetched from SNAP peers and cached briefly. Pin hot on-demand addresses in skim.yaml (skim_dashboard returns a ready-made block).

panels.title: Keys fetched from the network per address
panels.description: Steady fetching means the address is read often but not pinned.

panels.title: Subscription maintenance (per block)
panels.description: One subscription pass after each applied block: declared keys, calls, readiness. P99 should stay flat as subscribed and archived keys grow.

panels.title: Archive base writes
panels.description: One redb commit each. Expected near 0 once archived keys have their base: re-subscribing a based key writes nothing.

panels.title: Retained data by structure (stacked) vs RSS
panels.description: Estimated payload bytes each structure holds (skim_memory_bytes). The gap to RSS is allocator overhead, code pages and what isn't counted: a heap profile explains it. A part that keeps rising after its cache is full points at a leak.

panels.title: Entries by structure
panels.description: Blocks, keys or peers each structure holds. Fixed-size caches level off once full (tx index after 2,048 blocks, headers after 8,192).
